text:
amira: quick sync thread — building a concrete spec for the 'isolation waves' roadmap and the routing policy contract. goal: unambiguous launch gates and owner commitments.
rafi: high level take: make waves data-driven and reversible. prefer guardrails over hard locks. propose three enforcement primitives: routing tags, eviction-buckets, and fallback chains.
noor: infra constraints: burst buffer size, cross-region egress cap, and pre-warmed shard counts per tier. we need these numbers per wave or we'll under/overprovision.
chao: SRE asks: include experiment metrics and an automated SLA burn dashboard. key indicators: p95 latency delta, error-rate per tenant, cache hit curve, and fallback percent. want alerts at 3x baseline error-rate and when fallback percent >2%.
amira: launch gate sketch (draft):
- Gate 0: lab canary (internal prod traffic <0.5%) for 48h, no P1s
- Gate 1: customer pilot (wave A): up to 10 customers, opt-in; perf p95 +5% allowed, fallback <=1% of requests
- Gate 2: broad pilots (wave B): 10-50 customers, region-aware routing enabled, cross-region egress <5% of their traffic
- Gate 3: GA (wave C): commercial customers with contracts, legal + compliance signoff, SLA adjustments
sam: ops playbook items to include for each gate: contact list, rollback steps, customer comm templates, credit/compensation policy, and a smoke-test checklist.
rafi: rough routing policy snippet (policy-as-yaml idea):
```yaml
kind: RoutingPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-isolation-v1
spec:
  priorities: [region_affinity, eviction_bucket, cost_class]
  fallback_chain:
    - model: quantized-lite
      max_latency_ms: 300
    - pool: regional-aux
      cross_region_ok: false
    - pool: shared-economy
  eviction_buckets:
    - name: burst
      budget: 0.15
    - name: steady
      budget: 0.85
  metrics: [p95_latency, fallback_pct, cache_hit_rate]
```
rafi: this YAML lets product specify behavior per-tenant and infra enforce budgets.
noor: question: do we allow per-tenant region pins at Wave 1? i'd vote no, Wave 2 yes with strict egress caps. pinning requires larger reserved capacity.
amira: agreed. plan: Wave 1 = global best-effort, Wave 2 = region-aware opt-in, Wave 3 = contractual pinning. add a "safety hold" flag for legal/regulatory tenants so we can keep them off new routing rules until manual clearance.
chao: safety tests to add to the runbook: simulated network partitions, forced eviction of a shard, and cross-region throttling while maintaining <1% tail errors. also ensure warm-up script for KV caches runs during migration window.
sam: for prioritization: product will own Wave 1 pilot list, infra owns provisioning numbers, SRE owns runbook. timeline ask: 2 weeks to a Wave 1 alpha, 6 weeks to Wave 2 pilot.
amira: product acceptance criteria (to be used by exec for go/no-go):
- Observable telemetry shows p95 latency within +5% vs baseline for 7 days
- Fallback impact <=2% of requests and no customer-facing quality regressions
- Cost delta projection automated and shared with finance for top 50 tenants
- Runbook verified via chaos test and rollback <15 minutes
- Legal/compliance signoff for any tenant requiring data residency exceptions
rafi: also propose a soft-metric: developer ergonomics for routing DSL. if it takes >3 edits across teams to express a common tenant policy, we need to iterate the DSL.
noor: infra will provide a cost/latency tradeoff matrix per tier and a sample script to estimate per-tenant delta. need customer prompt samples by EOW.
amira: action items: raf i + noor pair to produce routing YAML + provisioning table by Thu; chao to author the chaos test cases; sam to compile pilot comms + opt-in legal template. i'll collate for Exec sync next Wed.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: isolation-policy-service v0.9 -> canary cluster at 2026-03-25T09:00Z
amira: thanks everyone — will follow up with a one-pager + acceptance checklist. if anyone wants to add gating conditions DM me.
